author: benjaminion
content: Hi All - I've posted [the agenda](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2305) for tomorrow's ACDC call. FYI, I do not plan to make any decision around FOCIL tomorrow, but we should use the time to explore options and express preferences. Participation from EL devs is also welcome. Decision making will be in two weeks, along with revisiting the other items in the Heze scope, with a goal of getting everything wrapped up in that call. For those unable to attend tomorrow (happy Thanksgiving!), I'll start a thread here for async input, so feel free to post links to blogs etc. Nevertheless, what is said on the call remains the most transparent and governance relevant, so please bear that in mind.

author: casparschwa
content:
Sharing Ethlabs' take on how to move forward with Glamsterdam: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/ethlabs-position-on-glamsterdam/30518

tl;dr:
- We recommend going ahead with Glamsterdam as is. This is a difficult trade-off, and the problems found are serious and valid. Much of the disruption comes from repricing state creation, which is a necessary step on Ethereum’s path to 1000x scaling. The only option to avoid this would be to remove EIP-8037 outright, but this would give up Glamsterdam’s roughly 3x higher gas limit, and only postpone the problem to a later hardfork. A secondary source of the disruption is the new state gas reservoir. Here changes to the EIP could address some of the concerns, but only for a subset of affected projects and at the cost of further months of delay. On net, in our assessment, neither of these options pass the cost-benefit test.
-  There are important lessons from Glamsterdam on how to improve future hard forks. We need to flag disruptive changes early and bring app developers in, scope impact analysis more carefully for sensitive EIPs, establish a shared understanding of which invariants app developers can rely on, and provide new primitives where there are gaps today, including those introduced by EIP-8037.

author: ajsutton
content: Just to flag "bring(ing) app developers in" means having done all the benchmarking required to have a "final" proposal early (obviously might change based on app dev feedback but shouldn't have pending validations or decisions from core devs remaining) and get the key tools like forge updated to implement it. Most projects have a battery of tests they can run to validate things but if they don't have tooling with the new standard they can't run them and depend on eyeballing/ai-balling the code to find what might be affected which is far less accurate.
